title: R’ Nehorai, an Amora
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Chullin 55b: he said in the name of Shmuel.

At the end of Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 71, R-A [ר״א] and R’ Nehorai dispute which tribe Elijah was from. R’ Nehorai says he was from Gad. R’ Pilipi bar Nehorai says, ‘What leads you to say so?’ He says to him, ‘For it is written,’ etc. It appears to Hyman that it should read, ‘R’ Pilipi said to R’ Nehorai.’ Hyman cites Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 18, and Tanna Devei Eliyahu Zuta, chapter 15, saying that there Elijah told him which tribe he was from. Hyman considers it very likely that this is the R’ Nehorai found in the Jerusalem Talmud, chapter 9, halakhah 2 [Berakhot by the separately read digital match], where, in Hyman’s account, Elijah asked Rabbi Nehorai [נהוריי], ‘Why were tremors and creeping creatures created?’; and at the end of Ruth Rabbah, chapter 3, where Elijah asked him [or: they asked Elijah], ‘What is this that is written, “And Shacharaim begot,”’ etc.

notes.text: The checked Bereshit Rabbah opens with Eliezer but later uses Elazar in discussing the same argument; both forms are recorded rather than claiming uniform manuscript evidence. Hyman omits the tractate of his Jerusalem Talmud reference.

The heading and all other unsupported personal titles remain R-prime; the ambiguous ר״א stays literal R-A, not an asserted Eliezer or Elazar. The whole saved Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2 scalar explicitly titles Nehorai with רבי in the earthquake question, so Rabbi is supported only for that cited occurrence; the tractate is supplied by this digital match, not by Hyman. The scalar does not inspect Hyman’s creeping-creature or Ruth parallels or prove identity. Bereshit Rabbah Eliezer/Elazar differences are inherited prior reports, not freshly inspected whole evidence. Hyman’s it-appears-that-it-SHOULD-READ correction replaces bar Nehorai with to Nehorai; his very-likely identification remains his conjecture. His questions and the Gad tribe meaning, indirect statement of Elijah’s tribe, and end-of-chapter locators remain. The Ruth שאלו אליהו subject stays ambiguous and מה דין means what is this, not a legal ruling. No printed image or correction history has been established; all source holds remain.

The consulted Chullin 55b names Rabbi Nehorai in Shmuel’s name. Bereshit Rabbah 71:9 has Pilipi bar Nehorai. Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah 18 and Zuta 15 have Elijah addressing assembled sages. The Zuta also includes the opinion that he came from Gad. The consulted Jerusalem Berakhot 9:2 passage asks about earthquakes, and the consulted Ruth Rabbah 4:1 makes Elijah the one who asks Nehorai about Shacharaim. The identification of the figures across the passages is Hyman’s proposal.
